You read the 5 vowels, the basis of the whole alphabet.
Japanese uses three scripts together: hiragana (sounds, for Japanese words and grammar), katakana (foreign words) and kanji (characters with meaning, from Chinese).
You start with hiragana: 46 basic signs. Each sign is a syllable.
The vowels are short and pure: a as in “father”, i as in “see”, u as in “put” (lips not rounded), e as in “pet”, o as in “pot”. The Japanese order is a-i-u-e-o.
